newsitem.title: USA: Santee Cooper restores S.C. power after storm.
newsitem.headline: Santee Cooper restores S.C. power after storm.

text.p: Santee Cooper, a South Carolina state-owned utility, has restored power to all but 5,000 customers in the Myrtle Beach area after Hurricane Fran roared past Thursday evening, a company spokesman said.
About 36,000 customers in the Myrtle Beach area lost electricity Thursday night when hurricane winds knocked trees into transmission lines, spokesman Jerry Stafford said Friday.

Crews continued to repair transmission lines and remove fallen trees and debris Friday morning, but the work was concentrating on smaller residential lines with larger circuits already repaired early Friday, Stafford said.
"We've got the feeders, and now we've got to respond to more local calls," he said.
Hurricane damage to Santee Cooper facilities, which serve about 106,000 customers in three coastal counties of South Carolina, was concentrated in the Myrtle Beach area.
"The situation got pretty fierce in Myrtle Beach. We just couldn't put our (repair) crews out there until early this morning because of the high winds," Stafford said.

Downed transmission lines reduced Santee Cooper's load factor to about 1,419 megawatts (MW) as of about 2100 EDT Thursday, compared with a more typical load factor of 2,203 MW at 2100 EDT Wednesday, Stafford said.
No Santee Cooper generation units were knocked out or damaged by the hurricane, he said.
Santee Cooper's service area was spared the worst of the storm's wrath as it veered slightly north Thursday. Earlier forecasts showed Fran heading straight for Myrtle Beach.
"We started out sweating bullets yesterday and we ended up dodging bullets as this thing turned a little north. We were very fortunate," Stafford said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
